records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Esau, that [is] Edom.
pieces: This is the account of the family of Esau, that is, Edom.

L.1: And these [are] the generations of Esau, that [is], Edom.

R.1: This is the list of Esau's family. Esau is also called Edom.

decisions.choice: the generations of Esau: a new section of Genesis
decisions.reason: This heading (toledot) marks the sections of Genesis (2:4; 11:27; 25:12, 19; 37:2). As with Ishmael (25:12-18), the line not chosen is listed briefly before the story returns to the chosen line, Jacob's (37:2).

decisions.choice: Esau, that is, Edom: the name from the red stew
decisions.reason: Esau was called Edom ("red") after he sold his birthright for red stew (25:30). Edom became the people and land south-east of the Dead Sea, Israel's close kin and frequent enemy (Numbers 20:14-21; Obadiah).

records.source: עֵשָׂ֛ו לָקַ֥ח אֶת־נָשָׁ֖יו מִבְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן אֶת־עָדָ֗ה בַּת־אֵילוֹן֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י וְאֶת־אָהֳלִֽיבָמָה֙ בַּת־עֲנָ֔ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן הַֽחִוִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Esau took his wives from [the] daughters of Canaan: Adah, daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
pieces: Esau married women of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite,

L.2: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,

R.2: Esau married women from Canaan. One was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite. Another was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah. Anah was the son of Zibeon the Hivite.

decisions.choice: Esau's wives: names that differ from the earlier lists
decisions.reason: Earlier Esau's wives are named as Judith daughter of Beeri and Basemath daughter of Elon, both Hittites (26:34), and Mahalath daughter of Ishmael (28:9). Here they are Adah daughter of Elon, Oholibamah, and Basemath daughter of Ishmael. Women could bear more than one name, or the lists may come from different sources; the text does not explain.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zibeon: Anah's father, so Oholibamah's grandfather
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "daughter of Zibeon", which can refer back to Oholibamah as a descendant. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read "son of Zibeon", agreeing with verse 24, where Anah is Zibeon's son. The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the Hivite: one of the peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: Zibeon is listed among the Horites of Seir in verse 20. Hivite and Horite may be related names, or the letters may have been confused in copying.

decisions.choice: granddaughter of Zibeon (B); Anah was the son of Zibeon (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the relationship as verse 24 gives it (m2).

records.source: וְאֶת־בָּשְׂמַ֥ת בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל אֲח֥וֹת נְבָיֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: and Basemath, daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebaioth.
pieces: and Basemath daughter of Ishmael, Nebaioth's sister.

L.3: and Basemath, Ishmael's daughter, the sister of Nebaioth.

R.3: Esau also married Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

decisions.choice: sister of Nebaioth: Ishmael's firstborn
decisions.reason: Nebaioth was Ishmael's eldest son (25:13). Esau's marriage into Ishmael's family is told in 28:9.

records.source: וַתֵּ֧לֶד עָדָ֛ה לְעֵשָׂ֖ו אֶת־אֱלִיפָ֑ז וּבָ֣שְׂמַ֔ת יָלְדָ֖ה אֶת־רְעוּאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And bore Adah to Esau Eliphaz, and Basemath bore Reuel.
pieces: Adah bore Esau a son, Eliphaz, and Basemath bore Reuel.

L.4: And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath bore Reuel.

R.4: Adah had a son named Eliphaz, and Basemath had a son named Reuel.

records.source: וְאָהֳלִֽיבָמָה֙ יָֽלְדָ֔ה אֶת־יְע֥וּשׁ וְאֶת־יַעְלָ֖ם וְאֶת־קֹ֑רַח אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י עֵשָׂ֔ו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלְּדוּ־ל֖וֹ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These [are the] sons of Esau who were born to him in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were Esau's sons, born to him in the land of Canaan.

L.5: And Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These [are] the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

R.5: Oholibamah had three sons: Jeush, Jalam and Korah. All these sons of Esau were born in Canaan.

decisions.choice: Jeush, as the text is read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has Jeish; the Masoretes' marginal reading, followed here, is Jeush, the form found in verse 18 and 1 Chronicles 1:35. The same note applies in verse 14.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח עֵשָׂ֡ו אֶת־נָ֠שָׁיו וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו וְאֶת־בְּנֹתָיו֮ וְאֶת־כָּל־נַפְשׁ֣וֹת בֵּיתוֹ֒ וְאֶת־מִקְנֵ֣הוּ וְאֶת־כָּל־בְּהֶמְתּ֗וֹ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל־אֶ֔רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And took Esau his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the persons of his house and his livestock and all his animals and all his property which he had acquired in [the] land of Canaan, and he went to a land away from Jacob his brother.
pieces: Esau took his wives, his sons and daughters, everyone in his household, his herds and all his animals, and all the goods he had gained in Canaan, and went away to another land, apart from his brother Jacob.

L.6: And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the people of his household, and his livestock and all his animals and all his property that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to a land away from Jacob his brother.

R.6: Esau took his wives, his sons and daughters, and all the people who lived in his household. He also took his animals and everything he had gotten in Canaan. Then he moved away from his brother Jacob to another land.

decisions.choice: to a land away from Jacob: the land is not named
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "to a land". The Samaritan Pentateuch and some ancient translations add the name, "to the land of Seir", which verse 8 supplies.

records.source: כִּֽי־הָיָ֧ה רְכוּשָׁ֛ם רָ֖ב מִשֶּׁ֣בֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו וְלֹ֨א יָֽכְלָ֜ה אֶ֤רֶץ מְגֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ לָשֵׂ֣את אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י מִקְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For was their property too much for dwelling together, and was not able [the] land of their sojournings to support them because of their livestock.
pieces: They had too much wealth to live side by side; the land where they were living as foreigners could not feed all their herds.

L.7: For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their sojournings could not support them because of their livestock.

R.7: The two brothers had too many animals to live together. There was not enough grass in the land for all their animals.

decisions.choice: too great for them to dwell together: as with Abraham and Lot
decisions.reason: The words echo 13:6, when Abraham and Lot parted because the land could not hold both their flocks. Again the one not chosen leaves the land of promise.

records.source: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב עֵשָׂו֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֵׂעִ֔יר עֵשָׂ֖ו ה֥וּא אֱדֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And dwelt Esau in [the] hill country of Seir; Esau, that [is] Edom.
pieces: So Esau settled in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.

L.8: So Esau dwelt in the hill country of Seir; Esau is Edom.

R.8: So Esau went to live in the hills of Seir. Esau is also called Edom.

decisions.choice: the hill country of Seir: the mountains of Edom
decisions.reason: Seir is the range south-east of the Dead Sea. Esau was already in Seir when Jacob returned (32:3; 33:16); here his move is told in full.

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תֹּלְד֥וֹת עֵשָׂ֖ו אֲבִ֣י אֱד֑וֹם בְּהַ֖ר שֵׂעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Esau, [the] father of Edom, in [the] hill country of Seir.
pieces: This is the account of the family of Esau, ancestor of the Edomites, in the hill country of Seir.

L.9: And these [are] the generations of Esau the father of Edom in the hill country of Seir.

R.9: This is the list of the families that came from Esau, the father of the Edomite people, in the hills of Seir.

records.gloss: These [are the] names of [the] sons of Esau: Eliphaz, [the] son of Adah, [the] wife of Esau; Reuel, [the] son of Basemath, [the] wife of Esau.
pieces: These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, son of Esau's wife Adah, and Reuel, son of Esau's wife Basemath.

L.10: These [are] the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz the son of Adah, Esau's wife, [and] Reuel the son of Basemath, Esau's wife.

R.10: These are the names of Esau's sons. Eliphaz was the son of Esau's wife Adah. Reuel was the son of Esau's wife Basemath.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיפָ֑ז תֵּימָ֣ן אוֹמָ֔ר צְפ֥וֹ וְגַעְתָּ֖ם וּקְנַֽז׃
records.gloss: And were [the] sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zepho and Gatam and Kenaz.
pieces: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

L.11: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

R.11: Eliphaz's sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

decisions.choice: Teman and Kenaz: names of clans and places
decisions.reason: Teman became a district of Edom known for its wise men (Jeremiah 49:7); Job's friend Eliphaz was a Temanite (Job 2:11). Kenaz gave its name to the Kenizzites, a clan connected with Caleb (Numbers 32:12). As in chapter 10, many names in this list are also clans or places.

records.source: וְתִמְנַ֣ע׀הָיְתָ֣ה פִילֶ֗גֶשׁ לֶֽאֱלִיפַז֙ בֶּן־עֵשָׂ֔ו וַתֵּ֥לֶד לֶאֱלִיפַ֖ז אֶת־עֲמָלֵ֑ק אֵ֕לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
records.gloss: And Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, [the] son of Esau, and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These [are the] sons of Adah, [the] wife of Esau.
pieces: Timna, a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, bore him Amalek. These were the descendants of Esau's wife Adah.

L.12: And Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, Esau's son, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These [are] the sons of Adah, Esau's wife.

R.12: Eliphaz also had a lesser wife named Timna. She had a son named Amalek. These were the grandsons of Esau's wife Adah.

decisions.choice: Amalek: ancestor of the Amalekites
decisions.reason: The Amalekites became Israel's bitter enemies, attacking them after the exodus (Exodus 17:8-16; Deuteronomy 25:17-19).

decisions.choice: the sons of Adah: her descendants, including grandsons
decisions.reason: "Sons" here includes Adah's grandsons through Eliphaz; Amalek, the son of a concubine, is counted with them.

decisions.choice: a lesser wife
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "concubine" (see 35:22).

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י רְעוּאֵ֔ל נַ֥חַת וָזֶ֖רַח שַׁמָּ֣ה וּמִזָּ֑ה אֵ֣לֶּ֣ההָי֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י בָשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were [the] sons of Basemath, [the] wife of Esau.
pieces: The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the descendants of Esau's wife Basemath.

L.13: And these [are] the sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife.

R.13: Reuel's sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the grandsons of Esau's wife Basemath.

records.source: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הָי֗וּ בְּנֵ֨י אָהֳלִיבָמָ֧ה בַת־עֲנָ֛ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֑ו וַתֵּ֣לֶד לְעֵשָׂ֔ו אֶת־יְע֥וּשׁ וְאֶת־יַעְלָ֖ם וְאֶת־קֹֽרַח׃
records.gloss: And these were [the] sons of Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, wife of Esau: and she bore to Esau Jeush and Jalam and Korah.
pieces: The sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, were Jeush, Jalam and Korah, whom she bore to Esau.

L.14: And these were the sons of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau's wife: she bore to Esau Jeush and Jalam and Korah.

R.14: Esau's wife Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon. She had three sons with Esau: Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

records.source: אֵ֖לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עֵשָׂ֑ו בְּנֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּכ֣וֹר עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֤וּף תֵּימָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף אוֹמָ֔ר אַלּ֥וּף צְפ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וּף קְנַֽז׃
records.gloss: These [are the] chiefs of [the] sons of Esau. [The] sons of Eliphaz, [the] firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
pieces: These were the clan chiefs among Esau's descendants. From the sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn, came the chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

L.15: These [are] the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

R.15: These were the leaders of the family groups that came from Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's oldest son, were the leaders Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

decisions.choice: chiefs: leaders of clans
decisions.reason: 'Alluf is the title of the head of a clan; it may be related to 'elef, a clan or thousand. It is used for the rulers of Edom in Exodus 15:15. These chiefs ruled before Edom had kings (verse 31).

decisions.choice: leaders of the family groups
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the chiefs were.

records.source: אַלּֽוּף־קֹ֛רַח אַלּ֥וּף גַּעְתָּ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף עֲמָלֵ֑ק אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֔וֹם אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָֽה׃
records.gloss: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These [are the] chiefs of Eliphaz in [the] land of Edom; these [are the] sons of Adah.
pieces: Korah, Gatam and Amalek. These were the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in the land of Edom, the descendants of Adah.

L.16: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These [are] the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these [are] the sons of Adah.

R.16: Korah, Gatam and Amalek. These leaders in the land of Edom came from Eliphaz. They were descendants of Adah.

decisions.choice: chief Korah: a name not among Eliphaz's sons
decisions.reason: Korah was a son of Oholibamah (verses 5, 18), not of Eliphaz (verse 11). The Samaritan Pentateuch lacks "chief Korah" here, and the name may have come in from verse 18 in copying; or a clan named Korah may have been linked with Eliphaz. The Hebrew text is followed.

records.gloss: And these [are the] sons of Reuel, son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These [are the] chiefs of Reuel in [the] land of Edom; these [are the] sons of Basemath, wife of Esau.
pieces: From the sons of Reuel, Esau's son, came the chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom, the descendants of Esau's wife Basemath.

L.17: And these [are] the sons of Reuel, Esau's son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These [are] the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these [are] the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife.

R.17: The sons of Reuel, Esau's son, were the leaders Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These leaders in the land of Edom came from Reuel. They were descendants of Esau's wife Basemath.

records.source: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י אָהֳלִֽיבָמָה֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֥וּף יְע֛וּשׁ אַלּ֥וּף יַעְלָ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף קֹ֑רַח אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֞י אָֽהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה בַּת־עֲנָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] sons of Oholibamah, wife of Esau: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These [are the] chiefs of Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, wife of Esau.
pieces: From the sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah came the chiefs Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the chiefs descended from Esau's wife Oholibamah, Anah's daughter.

L.18: And these [are] the sons of Oholibamah, Esau's wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These [are] the chiefs born of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau's wife.

R.18: The sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah were the leaders Jeush, Jalam and Korah. They were the leaders who came from Oholibamah, Anah's daughter.

records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Esau, and these their chiefs; that [is] Edom.
pieces: These are the sons of Esau, that is, Edom, and these are their chiefs.

L.19: These [are] the sons of Esau, and these [are] their chiefs; that [is], Edom.

R.19: These were the sons of Esau, who is Edom, and the leaders of their family groups.

records.source: אֵ֤לֶּה בְנֵֽי־שֵׂעִיר֙ הַחֹרִ֔י יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ לוֹטָ֥ן וְשׁוֹבָ֖ל וְצִבְע֥וֹן וַעֲנָֽה׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan and Shobal and Zibeon and Anah,
pieces: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, the people who already lived in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

L.20: These [are] the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

R.20: Seir the Horite and his family lived in that land before Esau came. Seir's sons were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

decisions.choice: Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: the people before Edom
decisions.reason: The Horites lived in Seir before Esau's descendants. Deuteronomy 2:12, 22 says the sons of Esau drove them out and settled in their place. Esau's family married into theirs (verse 2). Seir is here the name of their ancestor as well as of the land.

decisions.choice: the hot springs: an unknown word, probably springs of warm water
decisions.reason: Yemim occurs only here. The Latin translation took it as hot springs, and there are hot springs in the region east of the Dead Sea. Some ancient interpreters guessed "mules" (which fits the donkeys) or simply "water". A find worth remembering in a dry land.

decisions.choice: Dishon: the Hebrew spells the name Dishan here
decisions.reason: The two brothers Dishon and Dishan (verse 21) differ by one vowel. Here the Hebrew points the name as Dishan, but this list follows the order of verses 20-21, where Dishon comes before Ezer and Dishan, whose sons follow in verses 27-28. 1 Chronicles 1:41 has Dishon. The vowel points are later than the letters, and the name is read as Dishon.

decisions.choice: before any king reigned over Israel: Edom had kings first
decisions.reason: God had promised Jacob that kings would come from him (35:11), yet Esau's line has kings first, as Esau became great first. The line also shows that whoever gave the list its final form knew of Israel's kings; Saul was Israel's first.

decisions.choice: over the sons of Israel (L); over the people of Israel (B)
decisions.reason: Hebrew "a king of the sons of Israel" means a king of the Israelite people, so Literal and Balanced say "over".

R.32: Bela son of Beor was king of Edom. His city was Dinhabah.

decisions.choice: Bela son of Beor: the kingship was not handed from father to son
decisions.reason: None of the eight kings in the list is the son of the king before him, and each comes from a different city. Edom's kings may have been chosen or may have won power, rather than inheriting it.

decisions.choice: Bozrah: a chief city of Edom
decisions.reason: Bozrah, south-east of the Dead Sea, was later a capital of Edom, named in the prophets' words against Edom (Isaiah 34:6; 63:1; Amos 1:12).

pieces: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who beat the Midianites in battle in the land of Moab, became king in his place. His city was named Avith.

L.35: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city [was] Avith.

R.35: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad became king. He had defeated the Midianites in a battle in the land of Moab. His city was Avith.

decisions.choice: defeated Midian in the country of Moab: the one deed recorded in the list
decisions.reason: Midian was a desert people descended from Abraham and Keturah (25:2). Edom, Moab and Midian lived near one another east and south of the Dead Sea, and their wars are known only from such brief notes.

decisions.reason: "The River" usually means the Euphrates (31:21), but that is far from Edom. Here it may be a local stream such as the brook Zered on Edom's border.

pieces: When Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, Hadar became king in his place. His city was named Pau, and his wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.

L.39: And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place; and the name of his city [was] Pau, and the name of his wife [was] Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

R.39: When Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, Hadar became king. His city was Pau. His wife was Mehetabel. She was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Mezahab.

decisions.choice: Hadar, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 1:50, the Samaritan Pentateuch and many Hebrew manuscripts read Hadad. In Hebrew the letters for d and r are very alike. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Mehetabel, the last king's wife: the only woman named among the kings
decisions.reason: The list stops with Hadar and names his wife, perhaps because he was still reigning when the list was drawn up. Mezahab ("waters of gold") may be a person or a place.

decisions.choice: granddaughter of Mezahab
decisions.reason: "Daughter" here means descendant; Balanced and Readable say granddaughter, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: by their clans, by their places: a list of clan territories
decisions.reason: This second list names chiefdoms by region. Some names match people already listed (Timna, Oholibamah, Kenaz, Teman), so they are probably clans and districts named after ancestors, not new persons.

decisions.reason: Esau's descendants already hold a land of their own, while Jacob's family still lives in Canaan as foreigners (37:1). Later God tells Israel not to take Edom's land, for he gave Seir to Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5).
